text:
maria: FYI — BlackTrail (dedicated customer) just pushed back on our standard 15% commit buffer for Q3. They want to try 5% to lower their committed spend. Can we run a quick risk/impact sim on GPU-hours, tail latency, and burst availability?

jia: I can run a sim. Need the traffic profile (p50/p95 token/sec, diurnal seasonality) and their current commit (GPU-hours/day).

maria: They committed 2,400 GPU-hours/month (roughly 80 GPU-hours/day). P95 peaks about 6x baseline during midday for business analytics jobs. Seasonality: +30% in October–November due to marketing campaigns.

sam: Important to consider region constraints — BlackTrail's primary region is eu-west-1 where we already have two full tranches next quarter. Less headroom. Dropping buffer to 5% reduces our spare capacity for microbursts and increases fallbacks to shared pool.

jia: Ok running a baseline Monte Carlo with current profile. Assumptions: Poisson arrival for sessions, job length ~ lognormal (mu=3.1, sigma=1.2), prefetched KV hits assumed 10% which reduces tokens by ~12%. Will simulate 90-day window including October uptick.

ops-bot: simulation queued (job id: sim-9742). ETA ~ 22m. Resources allocated on infra-sim cluster.

maria: While we wait — thinking through policy options: 1) Accept 5% buffer but require automatic burst-fallback billing at 2x metered rate after buffer consumed. 2) Keep 15% buffer but offer a one-time credit for initial quarter. 3) Hybrid: 8% buffer + scheduled burst windows during campaign weeks. Thoughts? :thinking:

leo: Option 3 seems pragmatic. 8% keeps some headroom and scheduled burst windows avoid cross-tenant contention. Need to model cost delta for BlackTrail and our exposure.

jia: sim finished. Quick results (summary):
```
- 15% buffer: probability of fallback to shared pool over 90d = 2.1%
- 8% buffer: probability of fallback = 6.9%
- 5% buffer: probability of fallback = 14.7%
- Expected additional shared-pool GPU-hours if 5% buffer chosen = ~320 GPU-hours/month (peak months)
- Median tail latency impact when shared pool used: +28% tokens/sec slowdown for latency-sensitive jobs
```

sam: That 14.7% chance is non-trivial given eu-west tranche saturation. If they fallback and we don't have sufficient shared pool, routing will failover to other regions which adds cross-region egress and +40–60ms cold latency. For interactive usage that's rough.

maria: What about cost to BlackTrail vs us? How much would they save on committed pricing by dropping from 15%->5%?

jia: Ballpark: with their commit, dropping buffer reduces their committed add-on by ~7% of committed hours -> ~$18k/mo saving on their invoice. But expected metered burst charges during campaign weeks (if billed at 2x) could eat most of that savings if usage spikes align. Also our incremental risk cost (operational and potential SLO credits) could be ~$6–9k/mo on average given the fallback frequency.

leo: We should surface trade-offs clearly: cost savings vs reliability and cross-region exposure. Also include mitigation: scheduled burst windows (we can pre-allocate short-term tranches during campaign weeks) and stronger routing rules to favor same-region warm pools.

maria: Action items:
- jia: attach full sim CSV + run sensitivity to job length variance and KV hit rates (owner)
- sam: check eu-west spare tranche schedule and estimate potential short-term tranche we could rent from cloud partners for October (owner)
- leo: draft options & customer-facing language (including billing model for bursts)

jia: Uploaded sim CSV to the infra-share: https://redwood.internal/sims/sim-9742.csv and pushed a short notebook w/ plots. Key variable that flips decision: if job length sigma drops <0.9, 5% becomes borderline-acceptable.

ops-bot: reminder set for next check-in in 48h (thread: sim-9742 followup).

maria: Thanks all. I'll propose the hybrid (8% + scheduled burst windows for Oct/Nov) in the pricing call tomorrow and include clear rollback/fallback SLAs if cross-region failovers increase. :thumbsup:
